per_question.question: What medical loss ratio (MLR) must Medicaid managed care organizations meet under federal law, and how does NC implement this requirement?
per_question.agent_answer:
Under federal law, Medicaid managed care organizations do **not automatically have to meet a federally fixed minimum MLR** in every state. What federal law **does require** is that states ensure each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP **calculates and reports** an MLR under the federal methodology. If a state chooses to impose a minimum MLR by contract, that minimum must be **at least 85%**. See **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(a), (c)** in [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438) (current; I checked amendments in the corpus and the authoritative document remains 42 CFR Part 438).

## Federal requirement

### 1) Calculation and reporting are mandatory
Federal regulations require the state, through its managed care contracts, to ensure that each MCO, PIHP, and PAHP **calculates and reports** an MLR for each MLR reporting year using the method in § 438.8. That is the unconditional federal requirement. **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(a)**, [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438).

### 2) An 85% floor applies only if the state imposes a minimum
Section 438.8 then says: **if a state elects to mandate a minimum MLR**, that minimum must be **equal to or higher than 85 percent**. So the federal rule is:

- **Mandatory everywhere:** MLR must be calculated and reported.
- **Mandatory only if the state adopts it:** a minimum MLR, which cannot be set below **85%**.

See **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(c)**, [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438).

### 3) Federal oversight/reporting context
The broader Part 438 reporting and oversight structure includes state reporting duties to CMS and quality oversight mechanisms, but those sections do **not** change the core MLR rule above. See **42 C.F.R. § 438.535** and **§ 438.354**, [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438).

## How North Carolina implements it

Based on the NC Medicaid policy corpus I could verify, I **could not locate a North Carolina DHHS or clinical policy section in this corpus that sets out the state's MLR implementation terms for PHP/MCO contracts**. So I cannot confirm from the retrieved NC policy text here whether North Carolina:
- expressly imposes an **85% minimum MLR** by contract,
- requires remittances for falling below that minimum, or
- states its MLR enforcement terms in a publicly retrievable DHHS manual section in this corpus.

What I *can* say from the verified sources is that North Carolina, like any state operating Medicaid managed care under Part 438, must ensure through its contracts that managed care plans **calculate and report** MLR in accordance with **42 C.F.R. § 438.8**. [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438).

## Bottom line

- **Federal law:** Medicaid managed care plans must **calculate and report** MLR; a plan must meet **at least 85% only if the state has chosen to require a minimum MLR**. **42 C.F.R. § 438.8(a), (c)**, [42 CFR Part 438](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/part-438).
- **North Carolina:** I could verify NC is bound to implement the federal calculation/reporting requirement through managed care contracts, but I **could not verify from the NC policy documents retrieved here** the exact state contract term or public NC policy text establishing a minimum MLR or remittance mechanism.

If you want, I can next help locate the **North Carolina managed care contract language** or **state plan / waiver materials** that show whether NC sets the minimum at 85% and how remittances are handled.
